questions.question:
Two statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All cocks are bears.

All bears are horses.

Conclusions:

I. Some bears are cocks.

II. Some horses are cocks.

III. All cocks are horses.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow.
Only conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is given below:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8e62ccb99cda1b2bedb5b7dc32ec64ddc1337a9c5de7dd1fa5d2da63df265e9f.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some bears are cocks → True, as all cocks are bear, some bears will definitely be the cocks.

II. Some horses are cocks → True, as all cocks are bears and all bears are horses, some horses will definitely be the cocks.

III. All cocks are horses → True, as all cocks are bears and all bears are horses

Hence, all the conclusions will follow.

questions.question: The age of a father is twice the age of his son. Five years ago, the father's age was thrice the age of the son then what is the age of the son now?
questions.solution:
Let the age of a father = 2x

As per the given information,

The age of his son = x

Five years ago,

Age of father = 2x - 5

Age of his son = x - 5

The father's age was thrice the age of the son.

2x - 5 = 3(x - 5)

→ 2x - 5 = 3x - 15

→ x = 10

Hence, the age of his son is 10 years.
